executive-summary.title: Paperless-AI: SSOT Retrieval Broker + Visual RAG Integration
executive-summary.scope: Complete implementation of unified document processing pipeline with: - SSOT (Single Source of Truth) Retrieval Broker for normalized retrieval - Visual RAG sidecar integration for intelligent field detection - Small model optimization (accuracy-focused, not latency) - Sequential execution for deterministic behavior - Circuit breaker pattern for graceful degradation
executive-summary.current-status: ✅ Architecture designed and documented ✅ Expert agent deliverables completed (4 parallel agents) ✅ Documentation system updated ⏳ Implementation phase ready to begin
executive-summary.handoff-objective: Coordinate implementation of all remaining components across specialized expert agents using phased execution with explicit handoff between phases and agents.

constraint.implication: Use sequential execution to ensure deterministic behavior
Optimize context window usage for every call

Parallel visual element detection - must have 500ms timeout
constraint.implication: Max 5 concurrent sidecar requests per document

constraint.fallback: Circuit breaker gracefully degrades to Tesseract-only mode

component.name: SSOT Retrieval Broker
component.responsibility: Unified retrieval interface for all queries

stages.stage: Path Selection - Route to appropriate retrieval strategy
Parallel OCR Extraction - Visual OCR + Tesseract in parallel
OCR Reconciliation - Merge OCR sources with document-type awareness
Extraction - Structured field extraction from reconciled OCR
Visual Query Generation - Generate targeted visual queries for missing fields
Visual Query Execution - Execute visual searches via sidecar
Result Aggregation - Merge visual confirmations with extraction

component.outputs: - Unified normalized result schema - Field confidence scores - Visual overlay positions - Audit trail with provenance

component.name: Visual RAG Sidecar
component.responsibility: Visual question-answering for field detection and validation
component.capabilities: - Table detection and structure extraction - Image/figure detection and cataloging - Layout analysis (spatial zones, text blocks) - Visual Named Entity Recognition (Visual NER) - Bounding box calculation with pixel accuracy
component.integration-point: Stage 5.5: Query generation receives custom_field_taxonomy Stage 8: Visual query execution with dynamic k selection
component.constraints: - 500ms per image timeout (hard: 1000ms) - Circuit breaker protection - Exponential backoff: 100ms, 200ms, 400ms - Max 5 concurrent requests per document

component.name: Circuit Breaker Infrastructure
component.responsibility: Graceful degradation when Visual Sidecar fails

states.state: Normal operation, all visual operations allowed
Sidecar failing, skip visual operations gracefully

component.transitions: - 3 consecutive failures → OPEN state - 30 second cooldown before HALF_OPEN attempt - Successful HALF_OPEN query → transition to CLOSED - Failed HALF_OPEN query → transition back to OPEN
component.fallback-behavior: - When OPEN: Use Tesseract OCR + cached embeddings - No pipeline failure - Continue with extraction-only results

subagent.phase-2-context:
OBJECTIVE: Implement Tesseract OCR track in parallel execution
TRACK 2 RESPONSIBILITIES: - Fetch OCR text from Paperless-ngx `/api/documents/{id}/` endpoint - Extract `content` field for Tesseract OCR output - Execute in PARALLEL with Visual OCR track - Apply document metadata for reconciliation hinting
INTEGRATION POINTS: 1. Load document type (scanned vs. digital) from Paperless API 2. Fetch existing Tesseract OCR if available 3. Pass to mergeOcrResults() for reconciliation 4. Document-type awareness: scanned docs favor Visual OCR in reconciliation
CONSTRAINTS: - Parallel execution with Visual OCR (no sequential dependency) - No additional timeout beyond circuit breaker - Caching for field taxonomy (TTL: 1 hour) - Handle API unavailability gracefully
SUCCESS CRITERIA: ✓ Tesseract OCR fetched without blocking Visual OCR ✓ Document type correctly identified ✓ Reconciliation biasing works (scanned docs favor vis_ocr) ✓ Cache hit rate > 80% for field taxonomy ✓ Zero API timeout failures
subagent.phase-3-context:
OBJECTIVE: Provide custom field taxonomy for query generation
DEPENDENCIES: - Phase 2 must complete (OCR done) - Field taxonomy must be loaded and cached
TASKS FOR QUERY GENERATION: 1. Expose custom_field_taxonomy for @agent-guidance-expert 2. Calculate field rarity (frequency distribution) 3. Provide field data types and validation rules 4. Track field mutations over time
OUTPUT TO PHASE 3: - Field metadata: { field_name: string, data_type: enum|text|number|date, rarity_factor: 0-1, frequency_in_taxonomy: number, validation_rules: array, suggested_queries: array }
USED BY PHASE 3: - Rarity factor drives dynamic k calculation - Data type informs query type (field_extraction|validation|exploration) - Frequency distribution creates logit bias weights

execution-protocol.instruction:
**STRICT SEQUENTIAL EXECUTION - NO DEVIATION**
Phase 1: CircuitBreaker Implementation ├─ Assigned to: @agent-pipeline-orchestration-expert ├─ Estimated: 2000-3000 tokens ├─ SUCCESS: All state transitions tested └─ SIGNAL: "PHASE 1 COMPLETE" → Proceed to Phase 2
Phase 2: Parallel OCR Execution ├─ Assigned to: @agent-pipeline-orchestration-expert ├─ Prerequisite: Phase 1 complete ├─ Estimated: 4000-5000 tokens ├─ DEPENDENCIES: │ ├─ CircuitBreaker.js (Phase 1) │ ├─ PaperlessService.js (already delivered) │ └─ Visual OCR via ollama_visual (qwen3-vl:8b) ├─ SUCCESS: Both tracks execute in parallel, reconciliation works └─ SIGNAL: "PHASE 2 COMPLETE" → Proceed to Phase 3
Phase 3: Visual Query Generation Integration ├─ Assigned to: @agent-guidance-expert ├─ Prerequisite: Phase 2 complete ├─ Estimated: 4000-6000 tokens ├─ DEPENDENCIES: │ ├─ Extraction results (field confidence) │ ├─ PaperlessService custom_field_taxonomy │ ├─ GuidanceTemplates system (already delivered) │ └─ CircuitBreaker (Phase 1) ├─ SUCCESS: 3+ queries generated, all valid for sidecar └─ SIGNAL: "PHASE 3 COMPLETE" → Proceed to Phase 4
Phase 4: Visual Query Execution ├─ Assigned to: @agent-pipeline-orchestration-expert ├─ Prerequisite: Phase 3 complete ├─ Estimated: 5000-7000 tokens ├─ DEPENDENCIES: │ ├─ Visual queries (Phase 3) │ ├─ CircuitBreaker (Phase 1) │ ├─ Dynamic K calculation logic │ └─ Visual RAG sidecar integration ├─ SUCCESS: Queries execute, results merge with extraction └─ SIGNAL: "PHASE 4 COMPLETE" → Proceed to Phase 5
Phase 5: Metrics and Monitoring ├─ Assigned to: Coordination (can run parallel with Phase 4 final stages) ├─ Prerequisite: Phase 4 implementation started ├─ Estimated: 2000-3000 tokens ├─ DEPENDENCIES: │ ├─ All pipeline stages (Phases 1-4) │ ├─ MetricsClient.js │ └─ Prometheus configuration ├─ SUCCESS: 11 new metrics registered, collection works └─ SIGNAL: "PHASE 5 COMPLETE" → Proceed to Phase 6
Phase 6: Testing and Validation ├─ Assigned to: @agent-test-agent ├─ Prerequisite: Phases 1-5 complete ├─ Estimated: 6000-8000 tokens ├─ DEPENDENCIES: │ ├─ All implemented components (Phases 1-5) │ ├─ Full pipeline operational │ └─ Visual sidecar available ├─ ISSUES DISCOVERY: │ ├─ Log failures in ISSUES_AUDIT_REPORT.md │ ├─ Sub-invoke @agent-debug-agent │ ├─ Wait for root cause analysis │ └─ Re-test after fixes └─ SIGNAL: "PHASE 6 COMPLETE - All Tests Pass" → Implementation Done

**CRITICAL: Stop BEFORE 28,000 tokens to allow continuation**
Token Budget Per Response: - Max output: 28,000 tokens - Safe stopping point: 25,000 tokens - Reserve: 3,000 tokens minimum
When Approaching 25,000 Tokens: 1. Finish current section/task 2. Generate COMPLETION CHECKPOINT 3. Explicitly state phase status 4. DO NOT continue to next phase 5. Request user to invoke next phase
Checkpoint Format (MANDATORY): ``` ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ PHASE [X] STATUS: [COMPLETE | IN PROGRESS | BLOCKED] AGENT: @[agent-id] | [Agent Name] ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
✓ Deliverables Completed: • [deliverable 1] • [deliverable 2] • [deliverable 3]
⚠️ Remaining Work (if any): • [item 1] • [item 2]
🔗 Next Step: Ready for PHASE [X+1] Invoke: @[next-agent-id] with context below
📊 Token Usage: ~[estimate]K / 28K tokens ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ```
Continuation Format (NEXT RESPONSE): ``` CONTINUATION: Phase [X] - Resuming from [checkpoint name] Previous completion: [what was done] Now resuming: [specific task]
[Continue with remaining work] ```

**EXPLICIT HANDOFF AT PHASE COMPLETION**
At end of each phase, include:
``` ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ READY FOR NEXT PHASE INVOCATION ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Current Phase: [Phase X - Description] Status: ✓ COMPLETE
Completed Deliverables: ✓ [file/component 1] ✓ [file/component 2] ✓ [test/validation 1]
Next Phase: [Phase X+1 - Description] Assigned Agent: @[next-agent-id]
Context for Next Agent: - Depends on: [list completed items] - Must deliver: [list expected outputs] - Success criteria: [acceptance criteria] - Estimated tokens: [estimate]
➜ INVOKE NEXT PHASE: @[next-agent-id]:
PHASE [X+1] INITIATED Triggered by: PHASE [X] COMPLETION
EXPERTISE REQUIRED: [Domain description from subagent registry]
CONTEXT FROM PREVIOUS PHASES: [Key dependencies and outputs]
PROCEED WITH: [Phase objectives] ```

**IF PHASE BLOCKED OR FAILS**
Immediate Actions: 1. Declare: "PHASE [X] BLOCKED" 2. Explain blocker: "Cannot proceed because [specific reason]" 3. Root cause: "Root cause: [detailed explanation]" 4. Recommendation: "Required action: [specific action needed]" 5. DO NOT skip to next phase 6. DO NOT attempt workaround 7. Escalate: "Awaiting resolution before proceeding"
Example: ``` ⛔ PHASE 2 BLOCKED
Blocker: Visual Sidecar unavailable Root Cause: ollama_visual service not responding Impact: Cannot execute Visual OCR track
Required Resolution: - Verify ollama_visual is running - Check network connectivity to sidecar - Confirm qwen3-vl:8b model is loaded
Status: Awaiting manual intervention before Phase 2 can proceed ```

**MANDATORY VALIDATION AT EACH PHASE END**
Before declaring phase complete, verify:
✓ All deliverables exist and are complete ✓ Code follows project style guidelines ✓ No TODO markers or incomplete sections ✓ Tests pass (unit and integration) ✓ Documentation is updated ✓ No breaking changes to existing code ✓ Backward compatibility maintained (where applicable) ✓ Error handling implemented ✓ Logging/metrics included ✓ No performance regressions
If any checkpoint fails: → Phase marked as "IN PROGRESS" → Specific issue documented → Agent continues fixing until all pass → Then marked "COMPLETE"

category.name: Architecture
category.criterion: SSOT Retrieval Broker successfully normalizes all retrieval paths → Visual, Text, Hybrid, and Expert queries all return unified schema → Acceptance: Sample queries from each type produce consistent output

Circuit Breaker prevents cascading failures → Visual Sidecar failures don't crash pipeline → Pipeline degrades to Tesseract-only mode gracefully → Acceptance: Sidecar timeout triggers OPEN state, pipeline continues

category.name: Performance
category.criterion: Parallel OCR execution: Both tracks complete within 1000ms → Visual OCR: ~500ms (budget: 500ms, hard: 1000ms) → Tesseract: ~300ms (API fetch) → Reconciliation: ~100ms → Acceptance: 95th percentile latency < 1s
End-to-end pipeline: < 2000ms per document → All 9 stages combined → Acceptance: P95 latency < 2s
Visual query execution: < 500ms per query (5 concurrent) → Max 5 queries executing in parallel → Total time: < 500ms for all 5 → Acceptance: P95 latency < 500ms

category.name: Accuracy and Quality
category.criterion: OCR reconciliation: Conflict rate < 10% → Divergence between Visual OCR and Tesseract → Acceptance: < 10% of fields flagged for manual review
Field detection: Precision > 0.95 → Extracted fields are correct (false positive rate < 5%) → Acceptance: Manual review of 100 documents shows > 95% accuracy
Field detection: Recall > 0.90 → Missing fields correctly identified (false negative rate < 10%) → Acceptance: Visual queries catch > 90% of actual fields on document
Field detection: F1 Score > 0.92 → Combined precision/recall metric → Acceptance: Calculated F1 from test suite > 0.92
Overlay position accuracy: ± 5 pixels → Bounding box coordinates match visual reality → Acceptance: UI highlights align with actual field position

category.name: Reliability
category.criterion: Zero deadlocks or race conditions → Parallel OCR tracks don't create timing issues → Circuit breaker state machine is thread-safe → Acceptance: 1000+ concurrent operations, zero deadlocks
Visual Sidecar availability: > 99.5% → Sidecar uptime monitoring → Graceful degradation when unavailable → Acceptance: Monitored over 7 days, > 99.5% availability
Graceful degradation: No pipeline failures → All failures are handled and logged → Extraction-only results are valid terminal state → Acceptance: 1000 documents processed, zero pipeline crashes

category.name: Integration
category.criterion: SSOT Retrieval Broker integrates with RetrievalBroker → Unified interface for all retrieval types → Intent classification routes to correct handler → Acceptance: RetrievalBroker tests pass
Visual RAG sidecar integration complete → Query generation → Execution → Result aggregation → Overlay positions calculable for UI → Acceptance: UI can render all field highlights
Database schema compatible → New tables created without breaking existing queries → Migrations execute without data loss → Acceptance: All existing queries still work

category.name: Documentation
category.criterion: All components documented → Code comments on critical paths → README files for each component → API documentation with examples → Acceptance: Zero undocumented functions
Operations runbooks created → Deployment instructions → Monitoring setup → Troubleshooting guides → Acceptance: Ops team can follow runbook successfully

communication-protocol.instruction:
**REPORT STATUS AT EVERY PHASE END**
Required Information: 1. Phase number and name 2. Completion status (COMPLETE / IN PROGRESS / BLOCKED) 3. What was delivered (specific files, functions, tests) 4. What passed validation 5. What issues were encountered and resolved 6. Token usage estimate 7. Ready signal for next phase (yes/no)
Format: ``` PHASE [X] STATUS REPORT ══════════════════════════════════════════
Phase: [X] - [Name] Status: ✓ COMPLETE
Deliverables: ✓ [File 1] - [Line count] lines ✓ [File 2] - [Line count] lines ✓ [Test Suite] - [Test count] tests ✓ [Documentation] - [Doc name]
Validation Results: ✓ Unit tests: 12/12 passed ✓ Integration tests: 8/8 passed ✓ Code review: Complete ✓ Documentation: Complete
Issues Encountered and Resolved: - [Issue 1]: [Resolution] - [Issue 2]: [Resolution]
Token Usage: ~6,500 / 28,000 tokens
➜ READY FOR PHASE [X+1]: YES ```

**IMMEDIATE ESCALATION IF BLOCKED**
When Phase Cannot Continue: 1. Stop all work 2. Document blocker clearly 3. Explain why phase is blocked 4. Recommend resolution steps 5. Request user intervention 6. DO NOT skip to next phase 7. DO NOT attempt workarounds without approval
Blocker Report Format: ``` ⛔ PHASE [X] BLOCKED ══════════════════════════════════════════
Blocker: [Specific issue]
Root Cause: [Detailed explanation]
Why This Blocks Phase: [Impact analysis]
Required to Proceed: - [Action 1] - [Action 2] - [Action 3]
Recommendation: [What should be done]
Awaiting: [Manual intervention / Code review / Deployment / etc.] ```

**PROTOCOL FOR @agent-test-agent FAILURES**
When Test Fails During Phase 6: 1. Log failure in ISSUES_AUDIT_REPORT.md 2. Include: Test name, expected vs actual, stack trace 3. Sub-invoke @agent-debug-agent with failure report 4. @agent-debug-agent performs root cause analysis 5. @agent-debug-agent creates fix recommendations 6. Original component owner fixes issue 7. @agent-test-agent re-runs test to verify 8. If test passes: Mark as fixed, move to next test 9. If test fails: Update analysis, iterate
Format for Issue Report: ``` ISSUE: [Component] - [Test Name]
Test: [test_name] Status: ❌ FAILED
Expected Behavior: [Description of expected result]
Actual Behavior: [What actually happened]
Stack Trace: [Error trace or assertion failure]
Affected Component: [Which phase/component]
Severity: [CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW]
Sub-invoked: @agent-debug-agent for analysis ```

small-model-optimization.principle: Small models (4.7-8.7GB) require different strategies than large models. Focus on ACCURACY, not speed. Use structured prompts and validation to compensate for model limitations.

strategy.name: Context Management
strategy.problem: Small models have limited context windows
strategy.solution: - Keep prompts concise and focused - Use guidance templates for structured output - Apply logit bias to guide token selection - Pre-process OCR text to remove noise before visual queries
strategy.implementation: ✓ All guidance templates use brief, focused prompts ✓ Visual queries are 1-2 sentences max ✓ Logit bias boosts JSON structure tokens ✓ OCR preprocessing removes duplicate/garbage text

strategy.name: Output Validation
strategy.problem: Small models more likely to produce malformed JSON or missing fields
strategy.solution: - Always validate output against schema - Apply JsonRepair on failures - Retry with alternative prompt on validation failure - Fall back to heuristic extraction if LLM fails
strategy.implementation: ✓ All LLM outputs validated against Pydantic schemas ✓ JsonRepair applied to malformed JSON ✓ Retry policy: 3 attempts with different prompts ✓ Fallback: heuristic field extraction

strategy.name: Sequential Execution
strategy.problem: Parallel operations increase likelihood of timeout/failure
strategy.solution: - Prefer sequential stages where possible - Only parallelize where circuit breaker protects (OCR tracks) - Implement conservative timeouts (500ms budget, 1000ms hard) - Cache results to avoid recomputation
strategy.implementation: ✓ Pipeline stages execute sequentially (except OCR tracks) ✓ OCR tracks protected by circuit breaker ✓ 500ms timeout for visual element detection ✓ Field taxonomy cached for query generation

strategy.name: Logit Bias Optimization
strategy.problem: Small models easily distracted by unlikely tokens
strategy.solution: - Use logit bias to guide token selection toward structured output - Boost JSON structure markers: {, }, [, ], :, " - Boost field names from schema - Boost enum values - Suppress common error patterns
strategy.implementation: ✓ All guidance templates include logit_bias configuration ✓ Token IDs identified for: JSON markers, field names, enum values ✓ Bias values calibrated: 1.0-5.0 range ✓ Tested on sample queries for effectiveness ✓ Fallback: no logit bias if configuration fails

strategy.name: Graceful Degradation
strategy.problem: Small models more likely to fail on edge cases
strategy.solution: - Never fail pipeline on LLM-related issues - Always have fallback: heuristic, cached, or extraction-only - Log degradation for monitoring - Continue with best-effort results
strategy.implementation: ✓ Visual query generation fails: Skip visual validation, continue ✓ Visual sidecar timeout: Use cached embeddings, continue ✓ Extraction fails: Use raw OCR text, continue ✓ Field detection: Return partial results, continue ✓ All degradations logged for analysis

strategy.name: Monitoring and Feedback
strategy.problem: Small models drift in accuracy over time
strategy.solution: - Track user corrections as signal of model drift - Monitor F1 scores per document type - Collect metrics on failure modes - Update logit biases based on real-world performance
strategy.implementation: ✓ User correction rate tracked (indicator of F1 score) ✓ Per-document-type accuracy metrics ✓ Failure mode categorization ✓ Weekly logit bias adjustment (exponential decay: 0.95x) ✓ Fine-tuning recommendations based on patterns

quick-reference.integration-point:
**Location:** Phase 2
**Flow:** ``` Start Parallel Tasks: ├─ Task 1: Visual OCR (qwen3-vl:8b via ollama_visual) ├─ Task 2: Tesseract OCR (from Paperless API) └─ Task 3: Visual Elements Detection
Wait for both to complete (or timeout)
Call: mergeOcrResults({ vis_ocr_text, tesseract_text, document_type, visual_elements })
Returns: { reconciled_text, conflict_rate, source_attribution, ocr_metadata } ```

**Location:** Phase 3
**Flow:** ``` Input: { extraction_result, // From Stage 5 ocr_text, // Reconciled from Stage 4 field_schema, // From PaperlessService.getFieldTaxonomy() visual_elements // From Stage 4 }
Call: GuidanceTemplate.visual_query_generator_de(input)
Returns: { visual_queries: [ { question, // Natural language query field_target, // Target field name expected_element_type, // field_extraction|validation|exploration priority, // 0-1 ranking confidence, // Expected confidence for dynamic rarity_factor, // Field rarity in taxonomy logit_bias // Token biasing config }, ... ] } ```

**Location:** Phase 4
**Formula:** ``` K = base_K * (1 + (1 - confidence) * 0.5) * (1 + rarity_factor)
Base K Values: - field_extraction: k=3 (high precision) - validation: k=5 (moderate) - exploration: k=10 (high recall)
Example: - Query type: field_extraction (base_K=3) - Confidence: 0.6 → (1 - 0.6) = 0.4 → factor = 1.2 - Rarity: 0.3 → factor = 1.3 - Final K = 3 * 1.2 * 1.3 = 4.68 ≈ 5 ```

**Location:** Phase 4 (Stage 8/9)
**Process:** ``` Input: { extraction_result, // From extraction (Stage 5) visual_queries, // From query generation (Stage 5.5) visual_search_results // From sidecar (Stage 8) }
For each visual search result: 1. Deduplicate overlapping boxes (IoU > 0.7) 2. Match to extraction result by field_name 3. If match found: - Boost field confidence score - Add visual confirmation flag - Add overlay positions to metadata 4. If no match found: - Flag as newly discovered field - Include in results for UI
Output: { ...extraction_result, fields: [ ...extraction_fields_with_visual_boost, ...newly_discovered_fields ], visual_confirmations: [...], overlay_positions: {...} } ```

**Location:** All phases
**Pattern:** ``` Level 1: Full Pipeline (all stages, all components) └─ If Visual Sidecar timeout ├─ Level 2: No Visual Queries (skip Stage 5.5) ├─ Use: Extraction + OCR reconciliation only └─ Continue: To next stages normally
Level 2: No Visual Sidecar (circuit breaker OPEN) └─ If visual query generation fails ├─ Level 3: Extraction Only ├─ Use: OCR reconciliation + extraction └─ Continue: To reasoning/validation
Level 3: Extraction Only └─ If extraction fails ├─ Level 4: Raw OCR (best source) ├─ Use: Highest confidence OCR text └─ Continue: With reduced confidence
Level 4: Minimal (never pipeline failure) └─ Return: Partial results + logs ```

**Location:** All phases
**Key Metrics to Track:** ``` Per Stage: - Stage latency (p50, p95, p99) - Success/failure rates - Error categorization
Per Component: - CircuitBreaker: state transitions, failures, recoveries - OCR: reconciliation conflict rate, source attribution - Visual Queries: generation success, execution latency - Sidecar: availability, timeout rate, success rate
Per Document: - Field detection accuracy (F1, precision, recall) - User corrections (vs predicted) - Processing time breakdown
System Level: - Sidecar availability (uptime %) - Field detection F1 trend (for drift) - User correction rate (for drift) ```

handoff-prompt.troubleshooting:
Queries taking > 1000ms, circuit breaker opening frequently
1. Sidecar service unavailable or overloaded 2. Network latency to sidecar 3. Large images requiring long processing 4. Query complexity too high
1. Check sidecar service status: `curl http://sidecar:8000/health` 2. Monitor sidecar CPU/memory: should be < 80% usage 3. Reduce image size: resize before sending to sidecar 4. Reduce query complexity: break into smaller queries 5. Increase timeout budget (if acceptable for use case) 6. Enable caching for repeated queries
- sidecar_availability (should be > 99.5%) - visual_query_latency_p95 (should be < 500ms) - circuit_breaker_state (should be CLOSED) - circuit_breaker_open_count (should be stable/low)
OCR reconciliation flags > 10% of fields for manual review
1. Visual OCR (qwen3-vl) quality issues 2. Tesseract OCR quality issues 3. Document type detection wrong (scanned vs digital) 4. Reconciliation thresholds too strict (20% divergence)
1. Check Visual OCR output: Is qwen3-vl:8b model loaded correctly? 2. Check Tesseract output: Verify Paperless-ngx OCR is working 3. Review document type detection logic: Verify metadata is correct 4. Adjust reconciliation threshold (if data supports) 5. Log samples of high-conflict documents for analysis 6. Fine-tune logit bias for Visual OCR prompts
- ocr_reconciliation_conflict_rate (target < 10%) - visual_ocr_confidence_scores (should be > 0.8 average) - document_type_classification_accuracy - reconciliation_flag_count_per_field_type
<issue name="Field Detection Accuracy Low (F1 < 0.92)"> Extracted fields have many false positives or false negatives
1. Query generation not targeting right fields 2. Custom field taxonomy incomplete 3. Visual sidecar not finding fields visually 4. Extraction logic has bugs 5. Logit bias not configured correctly
1. Review visual queries: Are they specific enough? 2. Verify custom_field_taxonomy is complete: Check Paperless API 3. Test visual sidecar manually: Query specific fields on test documents 4. Review extraction logic: Check for regex or parsing bugs 5. Check logit bias configuration: Verify token IDs are correct 6. Increase dynamic K for low-confidence fields 7. Collect user corrections and analyze patterns
- field_detection_f1 (target > 0.92) - field_detection_precision (target > 0.95) - field_detection_recall (target > 0.90) - per_field_type_accuracy (identify weak fields) - user_correction_rate (indicates accuracy issues)
Visual queries generated but not executing, or returning empty results
1. Sidecar not responding to queries 2. Query format incompatible with sidecar 3. Circuit breaker OPEN due to previous failures 4. Embedding model not loading correctly 5. Field targets don't exist in document
1. Check sidecar query format: Verify API compatibility 2. Test sidecar manually: Send test query directly 3. Check circuit breaker state: Should be CLOSED or HALF_OPEN 4. Verify embedding model: Check if clip-vit-large-patch14 is available 5. Review field targets: Verify they match actual document structure 6. Check dynamic K calculation: May be too low for search 7. Increase logging on query execution for debugging
- visual_query_success_rate (should be > 0.95) - visual_query_latency_p95 (should be < 500ms) - sidecar_query_response_rate (should be 100%) - circuit_breaker_state (should be CLOSED) - query_result_empty_rate (should be low)
Pipeline degraded to Tesseract-only, not recovering
1. Sidecar service completely down 2. Network connectivity issue to sidecar 3. Circuit breaker cooldown period active 4. Repeated failures on HALF_OPEN test
1. Check sidecar service: `systemctl status sidecar` or equivalent 2. Verify network: `ping sidecar-host` and check firewall 3. Check cooldown timer: Waiting for 30 second cooldown 4. Wait for HALF_OPEN test: Should automatically try after cooldown 5. If stuck: Manually restart circuit breaker 6. Check logs for root cause of initial failures 7. Once sidecar recovered: Circuit will auto-recover to CLOSED
- circuit_breaker_state (should eventually return to CLOSED) - circuit_breaker_open_count (increasing = stuck) - sidecar_availability (must return to > 0) - circuit_breaker_last_state_change_timestamp - time_since_circuit_opened (if > 30s + random backoff, investigate)
End-to-end processing slower than target (< 2s)
1. Visual sidecar responses slow (> 500ms) 2. Query generation taking too long 3. Extraction stage slow 4. Multiple retries due to failures 5. Database queries slow 6. Image preprocessing expensive
1. Profile each stage: Check stage-level latency metrics 2. If visual queries slow: Reduce query count or optimize queries 3. If extraction slow: Check LLM response times 4. If retries: Fix underlying failures 5. Optimize images: Reduce size before visual processing 6. Add caching: Field taxonomy, embeddings, results 7. Consider sequential vs parallel tradeoffs
- pipeline_end_to_end_latency_p95 (target < 2000ms) - stage_latency breakdown (identify bottleneck stage) - visual_query_latency_p95 (target < 500ms) - extraction_latency (should be < 500ms) - retry_rate (should be < 5%)
UI highlights don't align with actual field positions (> 5 pixel error)
1. Bounding box coordinates not normalized correctly 2. Image resolution mismatch between sidecar and UI 3. Coordinate system different (0-1 vs pixels) 4. Page number mismatch 5. Sidecar returning wrong coordinates
1. Verify coordinate normalization: 0-1 scale vs pixel scale 2. Check image resolution: Ensure consistency sidecar → UI 3. Validate page numbers: Correct page for each overlay 4. Test sidecar directly: Get raw bounding boxes 5. Implement coordinate validation in aggregation stage 6. Add visual testing: Automated screenshots comparing prediction vs actual 7. Consider applying calibration offset if systematic error
- overlay_position_accuracy (target ± 5 pixels) - coordinate_normalization_errors (should be 0) - page_number_mismatch_rate (should be 0) - bounding_box_iou_with_manual (ground truth comparison)
Pipeline consuming > expected memory during execution
1. Large image files cached in memory 2. Visual embeddings not cleaned up 3. Query results accumulating without cleanup 4. Memory leak in circuit breaker or state management 5. No garbage collection between documents
1. Profile memory usage: `node --inspect` for heap snapshots 2. Implement cleanup: Delete large objects after use 3. Stream large data: Don't load entire documents in memory 4. Reduce image cache: TTL and size limits 5. Garbage collection tuning: Adjust Node.js GC settings 6. Monitor per-document memory: Ensure cleanup between documents
- heap_memory_usage (track growth over documents) - heap_memory_peak (should not grow unbounded) - cache_size (field taxonomy, embeddings) - object_count (growing = leak indicator)
